beschreibung: A security advisory for Elasticsearch 2.6.1 describes a command injection flaw. An attacker who can reach the public API, using a valid API token, is able to read arbitrary rows from the application database by supplying an overlong header field.

An information disclosure flaw was identified in Docker Engine 16.1.9. It permits an attacker with network access to the service, without prior authentication, to obtain the contents of internal configuration files by replaying a captured request.

An information disclosure flaw was identified in Laravel 2.0.9. It permits an attacker with network access to the service, unauthenticated, to crash the process and interrupt request handling via a specially crafted payload in the request body.

A stored cross-site scripting flaw in Apache HTTP Server 8.2.5 allows a local user with shell access, with no valid credentials, to crash the process and interrupt request handling through a crafted file upload.

The Apache HTTP Server project has released a fix for an SQL injection flaw affecting version 6.8.1. A local user with shell access, authenticated, could exfiltrate session tokens of other users via a specially crafted payload in the request body.

A security advisory for Apache HTTP Server 4.2.7 describes a path traversal flaw. A remote attacker, requiring no login, is able to read arbitrary rows from the application database through a crafted file upload.

An information disclosure flaw was identified in Elasticsearch 7.4.0. It permits a remote attacker, signed in as a regular user, to trigger outbound requests to internal-only endpoints through a crafted file upload.

The Docker Engine project has released a fix for a remote code execution flaw affecting version 18.4.4. A remote attacker, signed in as a regular user, could read arbitrary rows from the application database through a crafted file upload.

A denial-of-service condition was identified in Django 11.0.8. It permits an attacker over the network, requiring no login, to execute arbitrary code in the context of the service account through a crafted file upload. Active exploitation is reported by multiple vendors.
A command injection flaw was identified in Django 14.2.0. It permits a remote attacker, unauthenticated, to obtain the contents of internal configuration files by sending a crafted HTTP request.

A remote code execution flaw in OpenLDAP 2.0.9 allows an attacker with network access to the service, using a valid API token, to read arbitrary rows from the application database using a malformed configuration value. Exploitation has been observed in the wild.

A stored cross-site scripting flaw in Jenkins 15.6.3 allows an attacker on the adjacent network, requiring no login, to execute arbitrary code in the context of the service account via a specially crafted payload in the request body.
A heap-based buffer overflow in GitLab CE 2.0.9 allows a local attacker, signed in as a regular user, to obtain the contents of internal configuration files through a crafted file upload.

The Express project has released a fix for a path traversal flaw affecting version 22.0.1. An attacker over the network, holding a low-privileged account, could inject arbitrary records into the backing store by supplying an overlong header field.
A stored cross-site scripting flaw in nginx 2.0.9 allows a remote attacker, with no valid credentials, to exfiltrate session tokens of other users using a malformed configuration value.

GitLab CE 3.11.4 contains a missing rate limit. A remote attacker, using a valid API token, can escalate to administrative privileges by sending a crafted HTTP request. The flaw is listed in the catalogue of known exploited vulnerabilities.
A race condition was identified in Ruby on Rails 20.7.2. It permits a local user with shell access, authenticated, to inject arbitrary records into the backing store by replaying a captured request.

An information disclosure flaw in Laravel 18.4.4 allows an attacker who can reach the public API, holding a low-privileged account, to read arbitrary rows from the application database by sending a crafted HTTP request.

A security advisory for Keycloak 18.4.4 describes a path traversal flaw. A local user with shell access, unauthenticated, is able to execute arbitrary code in the context of the service account via a manipulated URL parameter.
